question: As per Sample Registration System (SRS) Bulletin 2020, what was the difference between death rates of rural and urban India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1.3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Sample Registration System (SRS) Bulletin 2020 revealed that the death rate in rural India was higher compared to urban India.
 
• The rural death rate was recorded at 6.9 per 1,000 population, while the urban death rate was 5.6 per 1,000 population.
 
• The difference between the death rates of rural and urban areas stood at 1.3 as per the SRS Bulletin 2020.
 
• Death rates are influenced by factors such as healthcare access, lifestyle, and socio-economic conditions.
 
• This data highlights disparities in health infrastructure and living conditions between rural and urban regions in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sample Registration System (SRS):**

 
 
• SRS is a demographic survey conducted in India to provide reliable annual estimates of birth rate, death rate, and other vital statistics.
 
• It functions under the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Death Rates:**
 
 
• Access to healthcare facilities, nutrition, sanitation, and socio-economic conditions play a crucial role in determining death rates.
 
• Rural areas often face challenges such as poor healthcare infrastructure and limited access to emergency services.
 
 
 
• **Urban vs. Rural Health Disparities:**
 
 
• Urban areas typically have better access to healthcare facilities, emergency services, and sanitation.
 
• Rural regions may lack adequate medical facilities, leading to higher mortality rates.
 
 
 
• **Policy Interventions:**
 
 
• Government schemes like Ayushman Bharat aim to bridge the gap in healthcare access between rural and urban areas.
 
• Improving rural health infrastructure is a key focus area for reducing disparities in death rates.
